01.r: The questioners answer Jesus's question about the coin.
01.n: The present tense in a past narrative, kept here as in the KJV, ASV and YLT.

03.r: Their one-word answer: the coin belongs to Caesar.
03.n: A single genitive, literally 'of Caesar'. What it answers is the question in the verse before, which the brief does not show.

04.r: Jesus's ruling follows on their answer.
04.n: Abbott-Smith gives a use 'of consequent events, then, thereupon'.

07.r: Hand over what is owed to the one it belongs to.
07.n: The questioners asked whether it was lawful 'to give' (Matthew 22:17, on this page); Jesus answers with a compound, 'give back'. Abbott-Smith gives 'to give up or back, restore, return', and especially of debts and the like, 'to render what is due, to pay'. This study uses 'give back' here so the change of verb shows; 'render', the KJV's word and the register's alternative for an obligation, says the same thing.

08.r: Draws the ruling from their own answer: the coin is Caesar's.

09.n: A neuter plural article with a genitive, literally 'the (things) of Caesar'. The Greek does not say what those things are.

11.r: The one to whom his things are to be given back.

12.r: Joins the second half of the ruling to the first.

13.n: The same construction as in the first half: literally 'the (things) of God'. The verb 'give back' governs both halves.

14.r: Greek puts the article before 'God'; English does not.

16.r: Greek puts the article before 'God'; English does not.

17.r: The one to whom his things are to be given back.
